defects.what: The film never says on stage or in a caption that the 100 pilots and their scores (83 = 65 + 18, 8 of 10, +20 -> +10) are a constructed model. The beat is eyebrowed 'THE CASE · FLIGHT SCHOOL', the numbers sit under 'Kahneman: a landing is skill plus luck', and the on-film honest line ('the manager may help; one quarter cannot tell') is about the hook, not the data. Only the live page's honest block discloses the model. A viewer of the film alone takes model draws for flight-school data. Fix: one honest line on stage and in caption 14, as amdahl does ('a teaching model, not flight-school data'), or an eyebrow 'DECLARED MODEL · 100 PILOTS' on the count

The CASE beat carries no real number at all: the fixture is an anecdote (TK74) and every digit in it is from the model, so the 'one real worked example with real, sourced numbers' beat is missing; Galton's real data stays on the page
The red (top 10) and blue (bottom 10) connector lines cross through the 100-mark TOMORROW column; the picture is busy and the '+20 TODAY / +10 TOMORROW' brackets sit at the edge of it
Hook is five short dashes under two column heads; the stop comes from the caption

one_line: The count is right and the arithmetic holds, but the film passes off a declared model as flight-school data; say on the film that the pilots are a model and it ships.
